newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo c-bank could keep discount rate steady.
newsitem.headline: Yugo c-bank could keep discount rate steady.

text.p: The Yugoslav central bank may keep its discount rate for September unchanged despite a sharp rise in the interest rate on short-term bonds sold via the Belgrade bourse, a bank official said on Tuesday.
The National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) on Friday auctioned 30-day bonds with the annual interest rate of 102.88 percent.
The bonds' rate serves as a parameter in setting the discount rate which has remained unchanged at 4.5 percent per month since June.

"A higher rate on bonds does not necessarily translate into a higher discount rate. As long as we have stable conditions, there is no reason to make any correction in the discount rate," NBY vice-governor Ratko Banovic told Reuters.
After the jump in July's inflation to 6.6 percent from 3.3 percent the previous month, August brought a slowdown in price rises and there was now a stable price environment, he added.
"Summer months have not been so stable for years. Normally we would face disturbing price movements in July and August, exploding in September and October. But not this year."
"Therefore, as long as stability is maintained, there would be no changes in the discount rate," Banovic said.
Banovic said the bank chose to lift the interest rate on short-term bonds to drain surplus liquidity from the market.
"We simply realized that our (old) 60-day bonds with 60.7 percent annual interest rate were no longer attractive and we wanted to renew investor interest in those bonds," Banovic said.
"We have noticed an improved liquidity among banks and were afraid that it could spill over elsewhere. So we could not take a chance and decided to attract money again in our bonds," Banovic said.
There was no other reason for a higher interest rate on those bonds, he added. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
